sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: With these visas you can move to Australia if you are subject to persecution in your home country. These visas allow you and your family to live, work and study indefinitely in Australia.

sections.heading: Overview > You must
sections.text:
- enter Australia by the date on your visa
- you and your family members must obey all Australian laws

We usually grant this visa to people referred to us by United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) for resettlement in Australia.

Help with your visa

If you are getting help with your visa, before you pay someone, read information on Who can help with your visa application.

sections.heading: Overview > With this visa, you can
sections.text:
- stay in Australia permanently
- work and study in Australia
- propose family members for permanent residence

sections.heading: Overview > Cost
sections.text: There is no visa application charge for this visa

sections.heading: Overview > Processing time
sections.text: The decision process could take many months, or even years. The number of applications we receive for resettlement each year is far greater than available visas.

sections.heading: About this visa > With this visa, you can
sections.text:
- stay in Australia permanently
- work and study in Australia
- enrol in Australia's public healthcare scheme, Medicare
- propose family members for permanent residence
- travel to and from Australia for 5 years
- if eligible become an Australian citizen
- attend free English language classes through the Adult Migrant English Program

sections.heading: About this visa > How long you can stay
sections.text:
This is a permanent visa. It lets you stay in Australia permanently.

You become a permanent resident when you enter Australia.

For citizenship purposes, your permanent residence starts on the day you enter Australia on this visa.

sections.heading: About this visa > Include family
sections.text:
You can also add certain family members to your application at any time before we decide on your application.

For this visa, your family are:

- your partner
- your dependent children
- your partner’s dependent children
- other relative who is a dependant.

If your child is not dependent on you, they must apply for their own visa.

Family members who apply for the visa must meet our health and character requirements.

Family members who are not coming to Australia might also have to meet our health requirement.

It is important to declare all your family members, even if they will not be applying with you.

If you do not declare a family member in your application, you may not be able to propose them for a Humanitarian visa after you arrive in Australia.

If you or your children are granted an Offshore Humanitarian visa based on your vulnerability as a woman, you should sponsor your spouse (or if it is your children, their parent) under the Family stream of the Migration Program.

If you are granted a visa based on your vulnerability as a woman and the department establishes that you falsely claimed that you were a single woman, we may cancel your visa, and you will not be able to sponsor anyone for a visa. For instance, if you claim your husband is missing when he is not.

We will not prioritise spouses or parents of vulnerable women and their children for visa processing.

sections.heading: About this visa > Apply from
sections.text: You must be outside Australia when you apply. You must also be outside Australia when your visa is granted.

sections.heading: About this visa > Processing times
sections.text:
We generally acknowledge Humanitarian visa applications in writing. Processing times can vary according to the applicant’s:

- circumstances
- location
- ability to travel
- ability to provide documents
- access to Australian government officials.

The decision process takes many months, even years. The number of applications we receive for resettlement each year is far greater than available visas.

Your application can take longer to process if:

- your application form is not filled in correctly
- you do not include all the documents we need, or we need more information from you
- it takes us time to verify your information.

Processing times also vary according to individual and family circumstances, such as health conditions that might require testing or treatment.

We will contact you at key stages of processing and when a decision is made.

Priority processing

The Australian Government has established policy to guide decisions on which applications we should generally give priority. This policy includes those who are outside their home country and are one of following:

- assessed as a refugee by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and referred to Australia for resettlement, or
- proposed by immediate family member (for example, spouse, child under 18) who holds a Class XB visa (subclass 200, 201, 202, 203 or 204) or close family member (for example, sibling, adult child, parent) who holds a refugee category visa (subclass 200, 201, 203 or 204).

Because of the limited number of resettlement places available each year and the high demand for them, we accept applicants in the most compelling circumstances only.

sections.heading: About this visa > Assisted Passage
sections.text:
The Assisted Passage program supports the delivery of Australia’s Offshore Humanitarian Program and provides health screening, travel and medical related services to refugee category visa applicants and visa holders.

The Assisted Passage service has transitioned from the International Organization for Migration (IOM) to Toll Remote Logistics Pty Ltd (Toll). Toll is responsible for delivering Assisted Passage services globally.

Toll will help you to attend health appointments and, if you are granted a visa, assist you to travel to Australia.

sections.heading: About this visa > Your obligations
sections.text:
You must enter Australia before the first entry arrival date (initial arrival date) specified in your grant letter.

If you signed a health undertaking, you must comply with it.

You and your family members must obey all Australian laws.

sections.heading: About this visa > Travel
sections.text:
The department will arrange your travel to Australia at no cost to you. If the first entry arrival date (initial arrival date) specified in your grant letter has passed, we may issue you with a travel facilitation letter. We may first ask you to undergo another medical examination.

You can travel to and from Australia for 5 years from the date we grant the visa. After 5 years you will need a Resident Return (RRV) visa (subclass 155) or (subclass 157) to re-enter Australia as a permanent resident.

sections.heading: About this visa > More information
sections.text:
The number of applications we receive for resettlement each year is far greater than available visas.

There are four visa subclasses included in the Refugee category of the Humanitarian Program. They are:

- Refugee (subclass 200)
- In-country Special Humanitarian (subclass 201)
- Emergency Rescue (subclass 203)
- Woman at Risk (subclass 204).

We will consider your application against each subclass.

You can find more information at Refugee visas (offshore).

sections.heading: Eligibility > Be living outside Australia
sections.text: You can't apply for this visa in Australia.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Face persecution
sections.text: You need resettlement because you face persecution in your home country.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet our health requirement
sections.text:
You and any family members who apply for the visa with you must meet our health requirement.

Family members who do not apply with you might also have to meet our health requirement.

If you have compassionate and compelling circumstances, we might waive your health requirement.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet our character requirement
sections.text:
You and any family members who apply for the visa with you must meet our character requirement.

Family members who do not apply with you might also have to meet our character requirement.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Sign the Australian values statement
sections.text: If you are 18 years of age or older, you must confirm you will respect the Australian way of life and obey Australian laws when you sign or accept the Australian Values Statement.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have paid back your debt to the Australian government
sections.text: If you or any family members (including those who don't apply for the visa with you) owe the Australian Government money, you or they must have paid it back or arranged to pay it back.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply
sections.text:
Check that you are eligible.

If you need help with your application, get someone to act on your behalf.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > Get help with your application
sections.text:
Only some people can help you with your application. If you appoint someone to give you immigration assistance they must be:

- a registered migration agent
- a legal practitioner, or
- an exempt person.

You can appoint anyone to receive documents on your behalf relating to your visa matter.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Provide accurate information
sections.text: Provide accurate information. See what happens if you can't prove your identity or don't provide true information.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Identity documents
sections.text:
Provide the pages of your current passport showing your photo, personal details, and passport issue and expiry dates.

Also provide:

- a national identity card, if you have one
- proof of change of name

Documents that prove a change of name include:

- a marriage or divorce certificate
- change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority
- documents that show other names you have been known by

If you can't provide these items, provide a statement explaining why you have no travel or identity documents.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Humanitarian circumstances
sections.text:
Please provide proof if you have registered with any international organisation dealing with refugees, such as the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).

If you have been referred for resettlement by the UNHCR, provide a full copy of your resettlement registration form.

Also write a statement, in English, about why you left your home country.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Visas or residence permits
sections.text: Provide certified copies of any visas or residence permits you hold.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Relationship documents
sections.text: Provide certified copies of marriage certificates or relationship registrations for you and anyone else included in your application, even if they are not joining you in Australia.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Photographs
sections.text:
Provide 2 recent photographs (45mm x 35mm).

The photographs should be of the full face against a plain background.

Print your name on the back of each photograph.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Character documents
sections.text: Provide military service records or discharge papers if you served in the armed forces of any country.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Tell us you are getting help
sections.text:
To nominate someone to:

- receive your correspondence, use Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- provide immigration assistance, use Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.

Send written notification or your forms with your paper application.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Partner documents
sections.text:
Provide:

- identity documents
- character documents
- documents about other relationships, if applicable
- any visas or residence permits held
- 2 photographs, as described in the information for the main applicant

Provide either:

- your current marriage certificate, or
- documents to prove you have been in a de facto relationship with your partner for at least 12 months before you apply

Documents that prove your de facto relationship include:

- joint bank account statements
- billing accounts in joint names
- joint leases or mortgages
- documents that show your partner has lived at the same address as you

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Dependants under 18 documents
sections.text:
For every dependant under 18 years old who is applying with you, provide:

- identity documents, or a statement explaining why they have no travel or identity documents
- proof of your relationship with them, like a birth or marriage certificate
- any visas or residence permits held
- any marriage certificates or relationship registrations held
- character documents, if applicable
- 2 photographs, as described in the information for the main applicant

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Dependants under 18 documents > Parental responsibility documents
sections.text:
Unless you have a court order you must get consent for the child to come to Australia from anyone who:

- has a legal right to decide where the child lives and
- is not coming to Australia with the child

They must complete either:

- Form 1229 Consent form to grant an Australian visa to a child under the age of 18 years
- a statutory declaration giving their consent for the child to resettle in Australia

Include a document with the signature and photo of the person who completed the form or declaration, such as a:

- passport
- driver’s licence

If the child is not staying with a relative or legal guardian, provide Form 1257 Undertaking declaration. The person they are staying with must sign the form.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Dependants over 18 documents
sections.text:
For every dependant aged 18 years or older who is applying with you, provide:

- identity documents
- documents about their other relationships, if applicable
- character documents
- any visas or residence permits held
- 2 photographs, as described in the information for the main applicant

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Dependants over 18 documents > Proof of dependency
sections.text: You must demonstrate financial, physical or psychological dependence.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Translate
sections.text:
Have all non-English documents translated into English.

Provide original and translated documents in your application.

Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters.

Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited. But on each translation, they must include their:

- full name
- address and telephone number
- qualifications and experience in the language they are translating

These details must be in English.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Certify
sections.text:
Have all documents certified. This includes:

- non-English documents
- English translations

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Keep a copy
sections.text: Keep a copy of your completed application.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Send
sections.text:
Send us:

- certified copies of all documents
- as much information as possible to help us decide on your application
- each document only once, even if you are using it to show more than one thing
- all documents with your application, if you can

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa > Apply online
sections.text:
Follow these steps to apply:

- Log in to ImmiAccount. If you do not have an ImmiAccount login, you will need to create a new account.
- Click ‘New application’.
- Click ‘Refugee & Humanitarian’.
- Click ‘Offshore Humanitarian Visa (200, 201, 202, 203, 204)’.
- Complete the application.
- Submit the application.

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa > Apply online > Have family applications processed together
sections.text:
Submit your visa applications and supporting documents together.

This helps give us a clear idea of everyone that is applying for a visa.

In your application, you must list all family members who are also applying for their own visa.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > What will happen after you apply
sections.text:
We will let you know when we have received your application and documents.

We will advise you if you are required to undertake a medical examination and or have your biometrics collected. Toll, the Department’s Assisted Passage service provider, will assist you with these requirements. If you are requested to undertake these requirements, further information can be found in the letters below.

- Requirements for your Offshore Humanitarian Visa Application - English
- Requirements for your Offshore Humanitarian Visa Application - Arabic
- Requirements for your Offshore Humanitarian Visa Application - Burmese
- Requirements for your Offshore Humanitarian Visa Application - Dari
- Requirements for your Offshore Humanitarian Visa Application - Hakha Chin
- Requirements for your Offshore Humanitarian Visa Application - Karen
- Requirements for your Offshore Humanitarian Visa Application - Nepali
- Requirements for your Offshore Humanitarian Visa Application - Persian
- Requirements for your Offshore Humanitarian Visa application - Somali
- Requirements for your Offshore Humanitarian Visa Application - Spanish
- Requirements for your Offshore Humanitarian Visa Application - Swahili
- Requirements for your Offshore Humanitarian Visa Application - Turkish

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Status updates
sections.text:
We can’t give updates on applications.

Wait for us to contact you. Ensure you keep us up to date with contact details and changes in circumstances.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Travel after you apply
sections.text: Do not arrange travel to Australia until we let you know, in writing, that we have granted you the visa.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Health exams
sections.text: We will let you know if you need health examinations.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Biometrics
sections.text: We might ask for biometrics (fingerprints and photo). We will let you know if you need to provide them.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Attach more information
sections.text:
If you did not attach all documents when you applied send them to the office where you sent the application, quoting the file number we have given you.

We might also ask you to provide more information.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Attend an interview
sections.text:
We might ask you to attend an interview. You must bring your passport or other identification and any other requested documents. You might be asked about:

- your situation, including why you are applying for a humanitarian visa
- your family
- information you provided in your application

If we receive information that could result in you being refused a visa, we will usually give you the opportunity to comment.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Add family
sections.text:
In some circumstances you can add certain family members to your application before we decide on your application.

Complete Form 1436 Adding an additional applicant after lodgement.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Mistakes on your application
sections.text:
Let us know as soon as you can if you made a mistake on your application.

Complete Form 1023 Notification of incorrect answers.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Help with your application
sections.text:
Let us know if you no longer want someone to:

- receive your correspondence - complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- provide immigration advice - complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.

Send written notification or your forms to the office your submitted your application.

For more information see Who can help you with your application.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Tell us if things change
sections.text:
Things you need to let us know about after you have applied include:

- changes to your phone number, email, address or passport
- changes to your marital or de facto status
- the birth of a child
- you want to withdraw your application

See how to tell us if your situation changes.

sections.heading: Step by step > Visa outcome
sections.text:
We will let you know our decision by email or letter.

New step description

sections.heading: Step by step > Visa outcome > About visa outcome
sections.text:
If we grant your visa, we will tell you:

- your visa grant number
- the date your visa starts
- your visa conditions, if applicable

Keep a copy of the decision.

If we refuse your visa, we will tell you:

- why we refused the visa
- whether you have a right to a review of the decision

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Coming to Australia
sections.text:
Before you leave

To find out about Australian history, culture, society and values, read the Life in Australia booklet.

You must arrive in Australia by the date specified in the letter we sent you when we granted your visa.

Other support

You can get help from the following organisations and programs:

Australian Cultural Orientation (AUSCO) Program

This 5-day program is free and open to all humanitarian visa holders over the age of 5. It is delivered overseas, to give you an understanding of life in Australia before you arrive.

Read more about the AUSCO program.

Humanitarian Settlement Program

This service will contact you when your visa is approved. It is free and runs across Australia. The focus is on helping you to learn English and to gain education or work skills.

Read more about the Humanitarian Settlement Program.

Departure health check

You, and any family members travelling with you on the visa, may be required to have a health check in the 72 hours before you leave for Australia.

The Australian Government will cover the cost of your health check.

The departure health check includes:

- checking that you are healthy enough to travel
- a physical check up
- a pregnancy test
- tests for communicable diseases
- vaccinations if needed, such as for measles, mumps and rubella
- treatment of parasites and infestations if needed

You must agree to follow up on any health conditions after you arrive in Australia.

Check your travel documents

You must have:

- a valid visa to enter Australia
- a valid travel document such as a passport or ImmiCard

At the Border

Completing an Incoming Passenger Card

All people arriving in Australia must complete the Incoming Passenger Card. You will get a card on board.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > In Australia
sections.text:
What can you do when you have this visa

- stay in Australia permanently
- work and study in Australia
- enrol in Australia's public healthcare scheme, Medicare
- propose family members for permanent residence
- travel to and from Australia for 5 years
- if eligible become an Australian citizen
- attend free English language classes through the Adult Migrant English Program

What you must do on your visa

You and your family members must obey all Australian laws.

Tell us if things change

Things you need to let us know about include:

- changes to your phone number, email, address or immicard
- changes to your relationship status
- the birth of a child

See what to do if your situation changes.

Travelling on your visa

You can travel to and from Australia for 5 years from the date we grant the visa. After 5 years you will need a Resident Return (RRV) visa (subclass 155) to re-enter Australia. To see when the 5 years ends, use VEVO.

Proving you have a visa

To obtain evidence you have a visa and show your conditions to someone, use VEVO.

Request your international movement records to get proof of your travel in and out of Australia.

Work and study

With this visa, you can work and study. You are protected by Australian workplace law. For more information on your workplace rights and entitlements see Visa holders and migrant workers.

Bringing family

As an Australian permanent resident, you might be able to sponsor eligible family members to come to Australia.

To find a visa for your family member, explore visa options.

You can also propose a family member for a Subclass 202 Global Special Humanitarian visa

Becoming an Australian citizen

After a certain time, you might be eligible for Australian citizenship. Find out more about becoming an Australian citizen.

For citizenship purposes, your permanent residency starts on the day you entered Australia on this visa.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Leaving Australia
sections.text:
Before you leave

Check your travel documents

You must have a valid travel document to leave Australia. Check your VEVO.

Ensure your visa is still valid and allows for re-entry to Australia

See what to do if your visa has expired or is about to expire.

After you leave

Proving you have been to Australia

Request your international movement records to get proof of your travel in and out of Australia.

sections.heading: Sponsor > About this visa > Scope
sections.text:
This permanent visa lets the applicant come to Australia if they are experiencing persecution in their home country. They must be living outside their home country and outside Australia.

Your applicant does not need to have a proposer for this visa. But it helps us to assess the support they would have if they were to in Australia.

You must be an eligible proposer to submit an application for this visa.

sections.heading: Sponsor > About this visa > Cost
sections.text:
Free

The Australian Government will cover the costs of medical and X-ray examinations for the visa holder.

If the application is approved, we will pay travel costs for the visa holder and their family.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Eligibility > Be an individual or an organisation operating in Australia
sections.text:
If you are an individual, you are:

- an Australian citizen
- an Australian permanent resident, or
- an eligible New Zealand citizen

You are not an eligible proposer if you hold a temporary visa.

If you are an organisation, you must be operating lawfully in Australia.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Eligibility > Meet our 'split family' provision, if applicable
sections.text:
In the past 5 years, you must have been granted a:

- Refugee visa (subclass 200)
- In-country Special Humanitarian visa (subclass 201)
- Global Special Humanitarian visa (subclass 202)
- Emergency Rescue visa (subclass 203)
- Woman at Risk visa (subclass 204)
- Protection visa (subclass 866), or
- Resolution of Status visa (subclass 851)

The applicant must be your partner, dependent child or, if you are not 18 or more years of age, your parent or step-parent (immediate family).

You must have declared the applicant as an immediate family member to us before your visa was granted.

If we grant the visa, it will usually be in the same category as yours. However if you have a Protection visa, then your family member will be granted a Global Special Humanitarian visa (subclass 202).

sections.heading: Sponsor > Eligibility > Not be an illegal maritime arrival on or after 13 August 2012
sections.text:
You did not come to Australia as an illegal maritime arrival on or after 13 August 2012.

New criteria description

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Before you apply
sections.text:
Check that you and the applicant are eligible.

New step description

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Gather your documents
sections.text:
You will need to gather and prepare the documents,

New step description

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Gather your documents > Proposer documents
sections.text:
Provide proof of your eligibility to propose the applicant, such as:

- Australian birth certificate
- certificate of Australian citizenship
- evidence of your permanent residence in Australia, or
- evidence that you are an eligible New Zealand citizen

If you are proposing as an organisation, provide:

- names of office holders
- a statement of the organisation’s objectives, activities and funding

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Gather your documents > Proposer documents > 'Split family' proposer documents
sections.text:
If you are proposing an immediate family member, provide:

- certified copy of your visa
- evidence of your relationship to the applicant, such as a certified copy of your marriage or birth certificate

If you have family members overseas who have fled from their home country and are vulnerable or under threat in their current country of residence, tell them to register with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).

New step description

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Translate
sections.text:
Have all non-English documents translated into English.

Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters.

Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited. But on each translation, they must include their:

- full name
- address and telephone number
- qualifications and experience in the language they are translating

These details must be in English.

Note: You do not need to have any documents certified.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > Scan or photograph
sections.text:
Scan or photograph all documents (English and non-English) in colour.

The scans and photos must be clear.

If a document is more than one page, save it all as one file.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Apply > Apply
sections.text:
Complete your sections of Form 842 Application for an Offshore Humanitarian visa and then complete and send it to the applicant to sign. Ask them to send the signed form back to you.

Complete Form 681 Refugee and special humanitarian proposal.

Submit both completed forms with us.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Apply > Apply > Apply online by email
sections.text:
Advantages of submitting online include:

- application processing times are shorter
- applicants’ information is not sent via inaccessible, unreliable or insecure postal networks overseas
- application costs are lower than if sent by post or courier
- reassurance that application has been safely delivered

Use our web form to email your application. [link to Email us your Refugee and Humanitarian visa application]

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Apply > Apply > Apply on paper
sections.text:
If you can't submit your application online, send it to us by post or courier. Include both forms and all required documents.

By post:

Special Humanitarian Processing Centre

Department of Home Affairs

GPO Box 9984

SYDNEY NSW 2001

By courier:

We do not accept hand-delivered applications.

Special Humanitarian Processing Centre

Department of Home Affairs

Level 3, 26 Lee Street

SYDNEY NSW 2001

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Apply > Apply > Living in regional Australia
sections.text: If you live in regional Australia, we might prioritise your application. A regional location is anywhere outside of Adelaide, Brisbane, Canberra, Melbourne, Perth or Sydney. Send us proof of your name and address, such as a utility, rates or telephone bill.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > After you apply
sections.text:
See what you can and must do after you apply

New step description

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > After you apply > After you apply
sections.text:
We will let you know when we have received your application and documents.

If we need more information, we will contact you.

New step description

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > After you apply > After you apply > Withdraw proposal
sections.text: You can withdraw your proposal before we grant the visa.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > After you apply > After you apply > Status updates
sections.text: We can’t give updates on applications within the standard processing time

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > After you apply > After you apply > Tell us if things change
sections.text:
Things you need to let us know about after you have applied include:

- changes to your phone number, email, address or passport
- changes to your relationship status
- you want to withdraw your application

See how to tell us if your situation changes

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Visa outcome
sections.text:
We will send you a letter or email to tell you if your application has been approved or refused.

New step description

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Visa outcome > Visa outcome
sections.text:
If your proposal is approved, we will send you a letter or email stating:

- the obligations you have as a proposer
- the date your proposal ceases

If your proposal is not approved, we will send you a letter or email stating:

- why your application was refused
- whether you can ask for a review of the decision and time limits

You can use VEVO to check the visa status and entitlements of people you have proposed.

sections.heading: Sponsor > When you have this visa > Your obligations
sections.text:
Your obligations

You must meet all these obligations. Even if you have authorised someone else to act for you, such as a migration agent.

Obligations related to the person you propose

If your applicant is granted this visa, you should be prepared to:

- meet them at the airport
- provide their accommodation on arrival
- help them to find permanent accommodation

You should also familiarise them with services and service providers, such as:

- banks
- Centrelink
- childcare
- education
- employment services
- healthcare
- permanent housing
- public transport
- translating and interpreting services

General obligations

You must:

- provide us with information if we request it
- tell us if things change
- obey the law
- continue to meet the eligibility criteria to be a proposer
- not give false or misleading information to us or the Migration Review Tribunal

Support for the person you propose

The Humanitarian Settlement Program will contact you with general information about supporting your applicant.

sections.heading: Sponsor > When you have this visa > Withdraw sponsorship
sections.text: You can't withdraw as a sponsor after we grant the visa.

sections.heading: Sponsor > When you have this visa > Tell us if things change
sections.text:
Things you need to let us know about after you have applied include:

- changes to your phone number, email, address or passport
- changes to your relationship status
- you want to withdraw your application
